claims.objects: An abstract block record over a supplied commutative coefficient ring: in rank two it stores a leading matrix, a modified-residue matrix, and a supplied exponent difference, while in every other rank it stores that rank and a proof that it is not two. The remaining objects are the free commutative monoid of these block classes and its natural-number-valued additive marker, smooth projective varieties through dimension four, smooth centers with their individual specialized QDM summands, projective-line stabilization, projective four-space, and a rationality predicate.
claims.hypotheses: The supplied relation called regular isomorphism preserves the entire zero-or-one marker weight; assumed weak-factorization data and marker formulas supply every blowup and blowdown formula while retaining the individual center summands; every summand from a smooth center of dimension at most two has zero marker; the cubic marker equals one; the projective-line formula doubles it; projective four-space has marker zero; and rationality supplies the birational comparison.
claims.conclusion: The stabilized cubic has nonzero marker, whereas projective four-space has marker zero; birational invariance therefore implies that the cubic threefold times one projective line is not rational.
claims.cautions: Conditional deduction. Lean defines the marker from the stored leading matrix and supplied exponent difference, constructs the quotient by the supplied regular-isomorphism relation, extends the marker to the free commutative monoid, proves the telescoping factorization argument with individual center summands kept separate, and obtains descent to birational classes. It does not prove that the stored matrices and exponent difference arise from a formal connection or from residue eigenvalues. Nor does it construct the cubic QDM, the Iritani or Iritani–Koto comparisons, weak factorization, or the geometric proofs of vanishing on low-dimensional centers. Those inputs remain explicit hypotheses of the formal theorem.

claims.objects: An additive marker on block multisets for smooth projective threefolds, a projective-three-space endpoint, a selected threefold, and a rationality predicate.
claims.hypotheses: Assumed weak-factorization data and marker formulas in dimension three supply the blowup and blowdown formulas; every point or curve center summand has zero marker; both endpoints are smooth of dimension three; projective three-space has marker zero; the selected threefold has nonzero marker; and rationality supplies the birational comparison with projective three-space.
claims.conclusion: The selected threefold is not rational.
claims.cautions: Fragment. Lean proves the endpoint contradiction while retaining each center summand separately, but does not construct the generic even QDM, identify a counted block with a nonzero additive marker, supply weak factorization or vanishing on centers, calculate projective space, or construct the rationality comparison.

claims.objects: A framed block retaining a marked small section and original-loop monodromy, the free commutative monoid of framed-block isomorphism classes and its additive primitive-sixth marker, smooth projective fourfold objects, smooth centers with their individual specialized QDM summands, projective-line stabilization, projective four-space, and rationality.
claims.hypotheses: Regular isomorphism preserves primitive-sixth multiplicity; the residual framed hypotheses supply comparison data retaining each center summand separately, together with vanishing of every such center contribution; the cubic marker equals two; the projective-line formula doubles it; projective four-space has marker zero; and rationality supplies the birational comparison.
claims.conclusion: The stabilized cubic has framed marker four; every rational smooth projective fourfold has framed marker zero; and consequently the stabilized cubic is irrational.
claims.cautions: Conditional deduction. The framed block presentation and additive marker are distinct from the residue presentation but invoke the same general birational-descent theorem. Lean does not construct the framed QDM comparisons or prove residual Hypotheses 5.7R and 5.7T; their exact formulas and vanishing statements for the separate center summands remain explicit hypotheses.

claims.objects: A parameter type indexing the family; one abstract family of varieties carrying an operation representing product with the projective line and a rationality predicate; a separate type of intermediate-Jacobian objects with predicates for smooth complex cubic status, algebraicity of the primitive minimal class, and universal CH0-triviality; and the hypotheses of the rank-two formal-exponent marker argument, with factorization data that retain the individual center summands.
claims.hypotheses: Every indexed fibre is a smooth complex cubic threefold whose intermediate Jacobian has algebraic primitive minimal class; Voisin's equivalence between that algebraicity and universal CH0-triviality, for every smooth cubic under consideration; preservation of universal CH0-triviality under product with the projective line; and, for every fibre, the hypotheses used in the one-stabilization marker theorem, including the projective-line marker formula and comparison with projective four-space. The existential form additionally assumes the parameter type nonempty.
claims.conclusion: Every fibre is universally CH0-trivial, its projective-line stabilization is universally CH0-trivial, and that stabilization is not rational; and, when the parameter type is nonempty, some cubic threefold with all three properties exists.
claims.cautions: Fragment. Lean checks the fibrewise separation composition but does not represent the moduli space, countable union of subvarieties, or codimension bound in the theorem type. It also constructs no Chow group, projective-bundle formula, intermediate Jacobian, primitive minimal class, or quantum connection. The existential statement rests on a supplied nonempty parameter type, and irrationality enters through the same hypotheses of the rank-two formal-exponent marker argument as thm:every-cubic. Because the codimension-three locus is a clause of the manuscript corollary but has no formal object or conclusion, this row is not graded as a conditional deduction.

claims.objects: An abstract variety with an operation representing product with the projective line and a rationality predicate; a supplied universal CH0-triviality predicate; an assignment of a defining polynomial in five variables over a nontrivial commutative coefficient ring; the notion of a decomposition of such a polynomial as a sum of polynomials in pairwise disjoint groups of at most three variables; the Fermat form; and the hypotheses of the rank-two formal-exponent marker argument.
claims.hypotheses: The almost-diagonal criterion, in the form that a variety whose defining polynomial admits such a decomposition is universally CH0-trivial; preservation of universal CH0-triviality under product with the projective line; the identification of the defining polynomial of the given variety with the Fermat form; and the hypotheses used in the one-stabilization marker theorem.
claims.conclusion: The projective-line stabilization of that variety is universally CH0-trivial and is not rational.
claims.cautions: Lean constructs no hypersurface, no Chow group, and no projective-bundle formula, and proves nothing about smoothness: the criterion enters as a premise about the supplied predicate, and the ground field of the geometric statement is not represented. What is proved rather than assumed is the combinatorial hypothesis of that criterion. Irrationality enters through the same hypotheses of the rank-two formal-exponent marker argument as thm:every-cubic.

claims.objects: An abstract variety with an operation representing product with the projective line and a rationality predicate; supplied predicates for universal CH0-triviality and for admitting a unirational parametrization of a given natural-number degree; and the hypotheses of the rank-two formal-exponent marker argument.
claims.hypotheses: The passage from two unirational parametrizations of coprime degrees to universal CH0-triviality; persistence of each parametrization degree under product with the projective line; unirational parametrizations of degrees two and three on the given cubic threefold; and the hypotheses used in the one-stabilization marker theorem.
claims.conclusion: The projective-line stabilization admits unirational parametrizations of degrees two and three, is universally CH0-trivial, and is not rational.
claims.cautions: Lean constructs no unirational parametrization, no decomposition of the diagonal, and no Chow group; the degree predicate is opaque and the criterion is a premise. Coprimality of two and three is the only arithmetic proved. The statement is about one supplied cubic threefold, asserts nothing about other members of the cited family, and addresses stable rationality nowhere. Irrationality enters through the same hypotheses of the rank-two formal-exponent marker argument as thm:every-cubic.

claims.objects: A parameter type; one abstract family of varieties used simultaneously by cycle and rationality signatures; a separate intermediate-Jacobian type; an operation representing product with the projective line; predicates for smooth cubic status, universal CH0-triviality, rationality, and family non-isotriviality; the hypotheses of the rank-two formal-exponent marker argument; an opaque period type and period map; and an opaque coarse-moduli type with the separated-variable and Eckardt predicates.
claims.hypotheses: For every parameter, the fibre is a smooth complex cubic threefold with algebraic primitive minimal class and the hypotheses used in the one-stabilization marker theorem hold. Voisin's criterion and preservation of universal CH0-triviality under product with the projective line are explicit premises. Non-isotriviality is not supplied as the conclusion: two parameters with distinct period-map values are supplied, together with the external implication from period-map nonconstancy to the family predicate. The exclusion clause supplies the Eckardt criterion, projective invariance, the pencil's Eckardt locus, and primitive data consisting of a chosen parameter, a chosen separated-variable model, its projective equivalence to that fibre, and the equality of the parameter's moduli point with the distinguished point.
claims.conclusion: Every fibre is universally CH0-trivial; every named projective-line stabilization is universally CH0-trivial and irrational; the family is non-isotrivial; and the separated-variable locus of the family in coarse moduli is exactly the distinguished point.
claims.cautions: Lean checks the final composition. It does not construct the A5-invariant pencil, its connected smooth locus, the invariant cubic space, its fibres, intermediate Jacobians, Chow groups, projective-bundle formula, primitive minimal classes, Voisin's criterion, direct QDM comparison data, coarse moduli, or period map. Irrationality uses the same hypotheses of the rank-two formal-exponent marker argument as thm:every-cubic. The period argument exposes a nonconstant map and a comparison implication rather than storing non-isotriviality itself as an input field. The separated-variable existence conclusion is constructed from the separately typed parameter, model, equality, separated-form, and equivalence data rather than stored as an existential premise.

claims.objects: The six-point permutation module of the alternating group on five letters over the prime fields of characteristic two and three, its augmentation quotient by the all-ones vector presented in four explicit coordinates, and the matrix commutant of the generated action on that quotient.
claims.hypotheses: Only the six-point action of the two generators induced by the label permutations `z + 1` and `-1 / z` of the projective line over the field with five elements; no geometric input.
claims.conclusion: In each characteristic the four-coordinate chart identifies the heart with the augmentation quotient and carries the two label permutations to the displayed generator matrices; every subspace stable under the generated action is zero or the whole heart, so the heart is simple; the commutant of the generated action is `{0, 1, W, W + 1}` in characteristic two, with `W ^ 2 + W + 1 = 0`, `W (W + 1) = 1` and the four elements pairwise distinct, hence the field with four elements, and consists of the scalar matrices alone in characteristic three, hence the field with three elements.
claims.cautions: The statement is about the concrete six-label model, whose labels are the six order-five subgroups of the concrete alternating group on five letters and whose generated action is that whole group; both facts are proved in this package but are not part of this terminal's type. The endomorphism algebras are exhibited by explicit generators and relations rather than by an isomorphism with named field objects. The manuscript indexes the module by the six conjugate order-ten dihedral subgroups of the alternating group, equivalently the six Sylow-five subgroups with their normalizers, which is a group-theoretic object this package does realize: it constructs the six order-five subgroups, proves that the two generators conjugate them by exactly the displayed label permutations, and computes each normalizer's order as ten. What keeps the row a fragment is therefore the two uncomposed identifications and the generators-and-relations presentation of the commutants, not a missing geometric input; identifying the labels with the six geometric axes is required by later statements, not by this one.

claims.objects: Lean represents the explicit five-by-five matrix 6I-J over an arbitrary commutative ring, vectors on five labelled coordinates, and the integral diagonal/off-diagonal parameters used in the human numerical derivation.
claims.hypotheses: For the augmentation assertion, the coordinate sum of the vector is zero. Parameter uniqueness assumes exactly the human proof's positivity d>0, invariant-sum equation d+5m=0, and intersection equation d^2-m^2=24.
claims.conclusion: The numerical hypotheses force (d,m)=(5,-1); the constant vector has eigenvalue one, every coordinate-sum-zero vector has eigenvalue six, and explicit mutually inverse integral row and column operations reduce the five-axis minor to diag(1,6,6,6,6).
claims.cautions: The elliptic quotient axes, coherent identifications, Rosati pairing, proof that this explicit matrix is the geometric Gram matrix, and non-CM generic-fibre passage are absent. The two typed numerical equations are supplied by unformalized imported inputs: the invariant-sum equation comes from the absence of a trivial summand in the five-dimensional constituent, and the intersection equation from Roulleau's intersection table (Theorem 11(D), Lemma 14, Corollary 16, and (3.1)) together with the Clemens-Griffiths minimal-class identity and the polarized Riemann-Roch trace formula of Grieve (Theorem 4.1). The generic-fibre isogeny from the fifth power of the elliptic curve to the intermediate Jacobian, asserted by the second sentence of the statement, is not constructed; Lean proves the Smith form of the matrix alone.

claims.objects: A base type with dependent fibre types named for the relative elliptic scheme, augmentation-lattice source, intermediate Jacobian, two-primary discriminant, H2 tensor two-torsion model, and isogeny kernel; a fibrewise integral first-homology realization consisting of a unimodular alternating polarization matrix for the Jacobian fibre, an integral comparison matrix, and the polarization pullback identity between them against the Kronecker product of 6I5-J5 with the standard alternating rank-two elliptic homology pairing, all indexed by an axis together with an elliptic homology coordinate; fibrewise coordinates identifying the two- and three-primary discriminant fibres with the two- and three-torsion kernels of that Kronecker polarization and the H2 tensor two-torsion and H3 tensor three-torsion fibres with four copies of the rank-two module over the respective prime field; the six-coordinate symmetric form 6*sum(x_i y_i) - (sum x)(sum y) and its normalizations modulo two and three; a fibrewise function, kernel inclusions, the explicit integral matrix 6I5-J5, an independently defined tensor-extended coefficient kernel over an arbitrary F2-module, standard rank-eight discriminant coordinates after choosing a symplectic basis, an explicit linear equivalence of those coordinates with two copies of the six-point coefficient heart, and the rational augmentation representation of the concrete six-point alternating-group action together with each labelled point stabilizer, its fixed subspace, and the linear group norm obtained by summing its ten coordinate-permutation operators. The three-primary branch additionally defines the four-coordinate model of H3 = Aug(F3^6)/<1>, its normalized symmetric coefficient form, the induced alternating form on two heart copies, and the vertical/scalar-graph packet. The permutation action is represented by explicit integral matrices: for each permutation of the six labels, its matrix in the five-coordinate chart, the contragredient matrix of that permutation, and the Kronecker extensions of both by the identity on the rank-two elliptic homology coordinate; equivariance of a comparison matrix for a permutation is the existence of an integral target matrix intertwining it with the source action. The transport terminal additionally considers an arbitrary type carrying an action of the concrete alternating group and an object fixed by one labelled stabilizer. The coefficient-descent terminal uses the rational six-coordinate permutation module, its constant line and quotient, the rational augmentation module, the six displayed axis vectors, their synthesis map, and the concrete alternating-group representations on the source and target. The integral quotient terminal uses the integral six-coordinate module, its constant line and quotient, the difference-coordinate chart to five integral coordinates, and the symmetric bilinear form induced by 6I6-J6. The discriminant layer adds the dual quotient of the integral source lattice by itself, presented as the cokernel of the source polarization on the standard lattice; the rational value (1/det F)(x^t adj(F) y) of two integral representatives; the Q/Z-valued discriminant pairing it induces on that quotient; orthogonal complements of subgroups for that pairing; maximal isotropy of such a subgroup, meaning that it pairs trivially with itself and no larger subgroup does; and the image in the discriminant group of the cokernel of a fibre comparison matrix under the matrix C^t T. The primary layer adds the torsion submodule of an integer, that is the classes it annihilates; the integral cofactor I5+J5 of the five-axis coefficient matrix and its Kronecker product with the inverse of the rank-two elliptic homology pairing; the two- and three-primary parts of the discriminant group; the orthogonal complement of a subgroup taken inside an ambient subgroup; and relative maximal isotropy, meaning isotropy together with maximality among the isotropic subgroups of that ambient subgroup. The comparison of the two two-primary models adds the entrywise reduction of integral vectors modulo two and the induced map sending the class of v to the reduction of C v. The pairing layer adds the adjugate of the source polarization and the normalized two-primary form on F2-valued source vectors, the dot product on axis coordinates tensored with the reduced elliptic homology pairing, together with the image of the two-primary kernel in the kernel of the reduced polarization. The standard-coordinate layer adds that image read in the four normalized heart coordinates with the rank-two tensor factor, as a subspace of the rank-eight model. Also the reduction modulo three of the cofactor image of a representative, as an additive map from the discriminant group to F3-valued source vectors; the normalized three-primary form on those vectors, minus the dot product on axis coordinates tensored with the reduced elliptic pairing; and the presentation of the three-torsion kernel of the polarization as two copies of the three-primary coefficient heart, one for each elliptic homology coordinate.
claims.hypotheses: Each fibre supplies explicit integral data: a Jacobian polarization matrix with determinant one, a comparison matrix, and the equation that the comparison pulls the former back to the Kronecker polarization of the six-axis source; and four coordinate equivalences, from the two- and three-primary discriminant fibres to the two- and three-torsion kernels of that polarization and from the H2 tensor two-torsion and H3 tensor three-torsion fibres to four copies of the rank-two module over the respective prime field. Propositions with no scheme-theoretic semantics are supplied for the remaining assertions of the relative lemma: connected smooth-locus status, the assertion that the displayed matrices are those induced on first homology by an elliptic scheme, the tensor-product source, the relative morphism, and the principal polarization, A5-equivariance, natural S6-actions, identification of the discriminant with the source-polarization kernel and of the tensor model with H2 tensor E[2], A5-equivariance of the discriminant identification, identification of the named kernel type with the two-primary kernel of the relative map, injectivity of its discriminant inclusion, and A5-stability of that kernel; maximal isotropy of the p-primary kernel is no longer supplied, being proved at lattice level. The geometric input also supplies, on every fibre, the first-homology form of that equivariance: the comparison matrix carries the source action of each of the two displayed generators of the six-label permutation group to some integral action of the target lattice. The geometric input also supplies, on every fibre, Frobenius marking of the transported two-primary kernel: the assertion that its packet class is moved by the Frobenius involution of the packet of diagonally stable halves. The selection terminal assumes one fibre's homology realization, that matrix-level equivariance, and that marking; the two packet terminals assume one fibre's homology realization together with that matrix-level equivariance and nothing else; the lattice-action terminal has no premise at all. The normalized-pairing terminal assumes only that one six-coordinate lift has vanishing coordinate sum, and the degree terminal assumes only the homology realization. The kernel-coordinate terminal additionally supplies an equivalence from each named discriminant fibre to the explicit rank-eight coordinates, a subspace whose vectors are exactly the coordinate images of the geometric kernel inclusion, and proofs that this subspace is diagonally stable and maximal isotropic. The three-primary coefficient terminal has no geometric premise: it works over the explicit field F3 with the displayed translation and inversion matrices. The discriminant-group terminal assumes only one fibre's homology realization, that is, the unimodular Jacobian polarization matrix, the comparison matrix, and the pullback identity; the pairing terminal has no premise at all. The primary-splitting terminal assumes the same single fibre realization and nothing else; its group-theoretic inputs are that six annihilates the discriminant group, which is proved from the explicit integral cofactor, and that two and three are coprime. The primary-order terminal assumes only one fibre's homology realization; it uses no equivariance, no marking, and no isotropy statement.
claims.conclusion: The Kronecker polarization of the six-axis source has determinant 6^8; every fibre comparison matrix satisfying the pullback identity has determinant of absolute value 6^4 and is injective on the integral source lattice; and both primary discriminant identifications D2 = H2 tensor E[2] and D3 = H3 tensor E[3] are constructed, agreeing in the supplied coordinates with the computed kernel equivalences of the two- and three-torsion polarizations. Modulo two the polarization reduces to the coordinate-sum map and modulo three to its negative, so each primary kernel is four copies of the rank-two module over the respective prime field. On a six-coordinate lift with vanishing coordinate sum the symmetric form is six times the dot product, its half reduces modulo two to the dot product, its third reduces modulo three to the negative of the dot product, and the form against such a lift is divisible by six, so neither normalization depends on the lift. The supplied geometric packet is packaged with a kernel-checked integral Smith witness for the five-axis Gram matrix, including explicit two-sided inverse row and column matrices and diagonal diag(1,6,6,6,6). Independently, for every F2-module T, Lean proves that the kernel of the tensor-extended five-axis Gram map is explicitly linearly equivalent to four copies of T. For a two-dimensional tensor factor it has 2^8 elements, and for scalar coefficients its coordinates agree with the normalized six-point coefficient heart Aug(F2^6)/<1>. The normalized dot product on that heart is proved bilinear, alternating, nondegenerate, and invariant under every word in the generated six-point action. After choosing a symplectic basis of the two-dimensional factor, the induced rank-eight tensor-product form is also proved alternating and nondegenerate, and every isotropic four-dimensional subspace is maximal isotropic. The explicit linear equivalence with two heart copies preserves this form and identifies the five projective-line packet members exactly with the diagonally stable maximal-isotropic subspaces of the rank-eight discriminant. In characteristic three, Lean constructs H3 as Aug(F3^6)/<1> and identifies it with four normalized augmentation coordinates. The quotient chart intertwines the induced translation and inversion actions with their displayed matrices and is an isometry for the minus-dot-product form descended through the constant line. The normalized symmetric form is nondegenerate and generator-invariant; the induced rank-eight tensor form is alternating, nondegenerate, and invariant under the diagonal generator actions. Exactly four four-dimensional subspaces are diagonally stable: the vertical half and three scalar graphs; all four are maximal isotropic. From the additional fibrewise kernel-coordinate input, Lean constructs an equivalence from every geometric kernel carrier to its displayed coordinate subspace and proves that every such transported kernel belongs to the five-member packet. Each labelled axis stabilizer in the concrete six-point action has ten elements and is the corresponding dihedral normalizer; its fixed subspace in the rational augmentation representation is exactly the line generated by the vector with coordinate 5 at that label and -1 elsewhere, and therefore has dimension one. The sum N of the ten stabilizer action operators has exactly that line as its range, satisfies N^2=10N, and after scaling by 1/10 is an idempotent projector onto the axis line. Every labelled axis stabilizer is self-normalizing. For any alternating-group action, if an object is fixed by the source stabilizer, then any two group elements carrying the source label to the same target carry that object to the same image. The six rational axis vectors sum to zero; their synthesis map has kernel exactly the constant line, is onto the augmentation representation, induces a linear equivalence from the six-coordinate quotient by the constant line, and intertwines the concrete alternating-group actions. Integrally, subtracting the sixth coordinate gives a linear equivalence from Z^6/Z1 to Z^5; the symmetric 6I6-J6 form descends through the constant line, and in this chart its Gram matrix is exactly 6I5-J5. Every permutation of the six labels induces a quotient map satisfying the identity and multiplication laws, and the descended form is invariant under all these maps. The discriminant group of the six-axis source polarization is finite of order 6^8, and its Q/Z-valued discriminant pairing is nondegenerate, vanishing on two integral representatives exactly when 6^8 divides x^t adj(A) y. For every fibre realization the cokernel of the comparison matrix embeds in that group through C^t T with image of order 6^4, and that image is isotropic, equal to its own orthogonal complement, and therefore maximal among isotropic subgroups, so its order is the square root of the order of the discriminant group. These are instances of a general theorem proved for an arbitrary integral alternating form of nonzero determinant pulled back from a unimodular form along an integral matrix, in which maximal isotropy comes from the adjugate identity C adj(F) C^t = (det C)^2 adj(T) rather than from a count of orders. The source polarization times the Kronecker product of I5+J5 with the inverse of the rank-two elliptic homology pairing is six times the identity, so six annihilates the discriminant group. Since two and three are coprime, that group is the direct sum of its two- and three-torsion parts, a class annihilated by a power of one of these primes is annihilated by the prime itself, so those parts are the primary parts, and they are orthogonal for the Q/Z-valued discriminant pairing, on which the pairing remains nondegenerate. For every fibre realization the lattice model of the isogeny kernel splits along the same decomposition, and each of its primary parts equals its own orthogonal complement taken inside the corresponding primary part of the discriminant group, hence is maximal among the isotropic subgroups of that part. These too are instances of a general theorem, proved for any module annihilated by a product of two coprime integers and for any subgroup of a discriminant group equal to its own orthogonal complement, with Bezout's identity in place of any count. The two models of the two-primary discriminant are identified. Reduction modulo two of the cofactor image is well defined on the discriminant group, kills exactly the three-primary part, lands in the kernel of the two-torsion reduction of the polarization, and is onto that kernel, so it restricts to an isomorphism of abelian groups from the two-primary part of the discriminant group onto that kernel and hence onto four copies of the rank-two two-torsion module in the normalized coefficient coordinates. The argument is division free, using only the cofactor identities F C = C F = 6 and cancellation of two and three in the integers. The discriminant pairing is computed across that identification. The adjugate of the source polarization is 6^7 times its integral cofactor, so the pairing of two classes vanishes exactly when six divides the cofactor form of two representatives; for two-torsion classes written as halves of polarization images, 2 v = F y, that becomes divisibility of y.(F z) by four, and the halved value reduces modulo two to the dot product on axis coordinates tensored with the reduced elliptic pairing, which is the normalized two-primary form of the manuscript. Hence the pairing of two two-torsion classes vanishes exactly when that form of their comparison images does, and the image of the two-primary part of the lattice kernel is exactly its own orthogonal complement for that form inside the kernel of the reduced polarization. The coordinate equivalence on that kernel is moreover an isometry from the normalized two-primary form onto the rank-eight tensor form of the coefficient heart, because a kernel vector's fifth axis coordinate is in characteristic two the sum of the other four, which is the fifth entry of the normalized heart representative. Carrying the two-primary kernel across that isometry therefore gives a subspace of the standard coordinates that is maximal isotropic for the rank-eight tensor form, and that subspace belongs to the five-member projective-line packet as soon as it is stable under the two diagonal generators. The two models of the three-primary discriminant are identified the same division-free way. Reduction modulo three of the cofactor image is well defined on the discriminant group, kills exactly the two-primary part, lands in the kernel of the three-torsion reduction of the polarization, and is onto that kernel, so it restricts to an isomorphism of abelian groups from the three-primary part of the discriminant group onto it and hence onto four copies of the rank-two three-torsion module. The discriminant pairing is computed across that identification: for three-torsion classes written as thirds of polarization images, 3 v = F y, vanishing of the pairing becomes divisibility of y.(F z) by nine, and the value (y.(F z))/3 reduces modulo three to minus the dot product on axis coordinates tensored with the reduced elliptic pairing, which is the normalized three-primary form of the manuscript. The comparison sends the class of v to minus the reduction of y, since two is minus one modulo three, and that form is unchanged by negating both arguments, so the pairing of two three-torsion classes vanishes exactly when the form of their comparison images does, and the image of the three-primary part of the lattice kernel is exactly its own orthogonal complement for that form inside the kernel of the reduced polarization. The coordinate equivalence on that kernel is moreover an isometry from the normalized three-primary form onto the two-copy polarization form of the three-primary heart, because a kernel vector's fifth axis coordinate is minus the sum of the other four, which is the fifth entry of the normalized heart representative. Carrying the three-primary kernel across that isometry therefore gives a subspace of two heart copies that is maximal isotropic and, by the half-dimension count in an eight-dimensional nondegenerate alternating space, four-dimensional, so it is the vertical copy or one of the three scalar graphs as soon as it is stable under the two diagonal generators. Both primary parts of the discriminant group therefore have their orders: each is carried isomorphically onto four copies of the rank-two module over its prime field, so the two-primary part has order 2^8 and the three-primary part 3^8, which factors the order 6^8 of the whole group into its prime powers. The six labels act on the source lattice: a permutation acts on coordinate families by inverse precomposition, its induced map in the five-coordinate chart has an explicit integral matrix, these matrices carry the identity to the identity and products to products, each preserves 6I5-J5, and the extension by the identity on the elliptic homology coordinate preserves the source polarization. The contragredient matrix, the transpose of the matrix of the inverse permutation, intertwines the polarization with the action and commutes in the same sense with the integral cofactor, so it descends to the discriminant group in its cokernel presentation. For a comparison matrix equivariant for one permutation, that descended action preserves the lattice model of the isogeny kernel and each of its primary parts, and the primary comparisons carry it to the reduced source action; on chart vectors of vanishing coordinate sum the reduced action is, in the four heart coordinates, the heart matrix of the same permutation, because such a vector is the difference presentation of the normalized heart representative of its own first four coordinates. Hence for a comparison matrix equivariant for the two displayed generators both transported primary kernels are diagonally generator stable, and with the maximal isotropy already proved the two-primary kernel is one of the five members of the projective-line packet and the three-primary kernel is the vertical copy or one of the three scalar graphs. Stability is no longer an input at either prime. Which member the two-primary kernel is cannot be settled by that action: the packet is exactly the set of diagonally stable maximal-isotropic subspaces, so every member satisfies the same group hypothesis. The input that settles it is Frobenius marking. For an equivariant comparison matrix whose transported two-primary kernel is marked, that kernel is one of the two exotic members, hence the graph of a slope annihilated by t^2+t+1 whose minimal polynomial over F2 is that irreducible quadratic, which is the coefficient-side slope datum of the marked finite-etale graph presentation at the prime two. The orders of the two primary parts of that lattice model follow: the whole model has order 6^4 and is the direct sum of its two- and three-primary parts, each part lies inside the corresponding primary part of the discriminant group, of order 2^8 or 3^8, so Lagrange's theorem forces the two prime-power factors of 6^4 apart and the two-primary part has order 2^4 while the three-primary part has order 3^4.
claims.cautions: Coverage is fragmentary, not a conditional proof of the manuscript lemma. The degree, finiteness, and two-primary discriminant conclusions are proved, but about integral matrices and finite modules: that these matrices are the ones induced by an elliptic scheme, the tensor-product source, the relative morphism, and the principal polarization is a supplied proposition with no scheme-theoretic semantics, so the lemma's geometry is assumed rather than constructed. The Smith witness, the tensor-kernel equivalence, the form properties, and the packet classifications remain unconditional statements about explicit objects that the supplied packet does not affect. Compatibility of the constructed two-primary identification with the geometric commutator pairing is not represented; what is proved about pairings concerns the explicit coefficient and tensor forms. The three-primary identification is coefficient-side in the same sense as the two-primary one: Lean computes the three-torsion kernel of the explicit polarization and transports it through supplied coordinates, but does not construct E[3] or its Weil pairing, identify the explicit heart and tensor form with the geometric discriminant, or prove that the actual geometric three-primary kernel is one of the four formal maximal-isotropic halves. The named geometric types, functions, and propositions do not define schemes, relative morphisms, geometric group actions, Weil pairings, polarization kernels, geometric tensor products, or maximal isotropy of the actual geometric kernel. The explicit tensor-kernel and stable-packet equivalences do not construct E[2], a torsion local system, its symplectic pairing, or the geometric classifying map into that packet. The kernel-coordinate bridge assumes rather than constructs the coordinate equivalence, exact kernel image, stability, and maximal isotropy needed to apply the five-member classification. The rational norm theorem concerns only the explicit coordinate representation; it does not construct or identify the manuscript's geometric norm endomorphism or identify its image with an elliptic subvariety of the relative intermediate Jacobian. claims.hypotheses: The projective classification uses only finiteness and the field axioms. The concrete F4 trace-determinant, maximal-isotropic, and group-order calculations have no added mathematical hypothesis. One marked-F4 specialization takes a continuous classifier into the discrete affine chart Option F4; a stronger specialization takes a continuous classifier directly into Projectivization F4 (F4 x F4). These assume that one chosen fibre is one of the two scalar graphs defined by the transported marked root and its root+1 conjugate. The strongest persistence terminal replaces that marked-pair premise by the weaker premise that the chosen projective point is not fixed by coefficientwise Frobenius. The concrete stable-half terminal universally quantifies a subspace of two heart copies and characterizes the exact condition that it have F2-dimension four and be stable under the diagonal translation and inversion actions. The stronger polarization terminal requires no additional premise: it characterizes packet membership by diagonal stability and maximal isotropy. The explicit projective-line equivalence and its five marked chart values require no additional hypothesis. claims.conclusion: Every projective-line point is uniquely vertical or a scalar graph; P1(F4) has five members and P1(F3) has four. The printed trace-determinant coefficient form and induced two-copy form are nondegenerate, every F4 scalar is self-adjoint, and every scalar graph equals its orthogonal complement, hence is maximal isotropic. Squaring on F4 is identified with the canonical Frobenius field automorphism; it fixes exactly 0 and 1, is involutive, and exchanges every other scalar with a distinct conjugate. On the affine projective chart it acts coefficientwise, fixes exactly the vertical point and graphs of 0 and 1, and its nonfixed locus is exactly the transported marked quadratic root together with root+1. Transporting that action through the proved affine-chart equivalence gives an involution directly on Projectivization F4 (F4 x F4), whose nonfixed locus is exactly the two scalar graph points of the marked root and root+1. The full five-letter symmetric group has order 120; its alternating subgroup has index two and full normalizer. Transported to this labelling, projective Frobenius is a transposition in the nontrivial coset, hence odd; its conjugation preserves both the alternating subgroup and the concrete PSL2(F4) projective image. A determinant unit whose multiplication preserves the trace against every test element is one. The concrete groups SL2(F4) and the alternating group on five letters both have order 60, the center of SL2(F4) is trivial, its faithful five-point projective image consists exactly of the even permutations, and the resulting construction gives an explicit abstract isomorphism SL2(F4) ≃ A5. Every continuous finite-discrete-packet classifying map on a connected base is constant, so membership in any distinguished subset at one fibre persists at every fibre. In particular, this is proved both for a continuous affine-chart F4 classifier and directly for a continuous classifier into the actual projective line when one chosen fibre lies in the marked two-point scalar-graph pair. More strongly, nonfixity under projective Frobenius at one fibre alone identifies that fibre with the marked pair and propagates the exact classification throughout the connected base. For the explicit six-point characteristic-two heart model, normalized representatives recover all four quotient coordinates, the coordinate kernel on the augmentation hyperplane is exactly the constant line, and translation and inversion induce the displayed matrices. The six labels are explicitly equivalent to the actual P1(F5); under this equivalence the two permutations are the projectivizations of (x,y) maps to (x,x+y) and (x,y) maps to (y,-x). These permutations preserve an explicit five-factor one-factorization; the induced factor words exhaust the alternating group on five letters and have exactly the same word kernel as the six-point words, so the generated six-point action is faithfully identified with a concrete A5. Lean constructs all six Sylow-five subgroups in this concrete A5 and proves that conjugation by the two generators acts on them by exactly the original six-point translation and inversion. The explicit P1(F5) labelling is therefore equivalent to the six-member Sylow-five packet. The faithful natural PSL2(F5) action has order 60; the two displayed permutations arise from explicit determinant-one matrices, and Lean constructs an isomorphism PSL2(F5) ≃ A5 that intertwines the full natural projective action with conjugation on the six Sylow-five subgroups. Both of these six-point actions are two-transitive. Every natural PSL2(F5) point stabilizer is proved to be the corresponding ten-element dihedral normalizer and is explicitly equivalent to D5. The six-label equivalence with the Sylow packet intertwines both generators with conjugation, and each point stabilizer is the corresponding normalizer. Each Sylow normalizer has ten elements and is explicitly equivalent to the dihedral group D5. Every subspace stable under both induced heart matrices is zero or the whole heart. A matrix commutes with every word matrix in the full generated heart action exactly when it is one of {0,1,W,W+1}, where W^2+W+1=0. A subspace of two heart copies is four-dimensional and stable under the diagonal generated action exactly when it is the vertical half or the graph of one of the four displayed commutant endomorphisms 0, 1, W, and W+1; the displayed packet has exactly five distinct members. An explicit equivalence with the actual P1(F4) sends the vertical chart point to the vertical half and the affine labels 0, 1, the transported marked root, and root+1 to the corresponding graphs of 0, 1, W, and W+1. The explicit alternating polarization form on the two heart copies is nondegenerate, and these five packet members are exactly the diagonally stable maximal-isotropic subspaces. The chosen linear equivalence from the standard rank-eight tensor discriminant coordinates to two heart copies preserves the bilinear form and transports this exact stable maximal-isotropic packet classification. Frobenius of the labelling field, transported to that five-member packet, is an involution whose fixed members are exactly the prime-field triple and which exchanges the two members of the exotic pair. On a graph member it squares the slope: the labelled commutant matrix of the Frobenius conjugate of a scalar is the square of the labelled matrix of that scalar. Hence for a packet member, being moved by the involution, which is what Frobenius marking asserts, is equivalent to lying in the exotic pair, and either exotic member is the graph of a slope annihilated by t^2+t+1 whose minimal polynomial over F2 is that irreducible quadratic. Marking is needed at one base point only: a continuous classifier from a connected base into the packet whose value at one point is moved by the involution is constant, and every fibre is one of the two exotic members. That involution is realized by the labels themselves. Scaling by the non-square scalar 2 is an odd permutation of the six labels, while the translation and the involution x to -1/x are even; permuting the labels acts on the four heart coordinates of any vector of the augmentation hyperplane through the displayed matrix of the permutation, for every word in the three generators; and the sign of the label permutation of a word is the parity of its number of scaling letters. The diagonal heart action of the scaling matrix on two copies of the heart is exactly the transported Frobenius involution of the packet, so a packet member is marked precisely when that action moves it. Every word whose label permutation is even fixes every packet member, and every word whose label permutation is odd acts on the packet as the transported involution, so the packet action of the group generated by the three displayed label permutations factors through the sign character of the six labels. In the other direction each of the three members defined over the prime field is fixed by the diagonal action of every invertible heart matrix, so a packet member moved by any such action lies in the exotic pair. The label group is now determined exactly. A permutation of the six labels preserves the packet if and only if conjugation by its heart matrix carries W to W or to W+1. The permutations whose heart matrix centralizes W form a group of order sixty, computed by the orbit-stabilizer theorem from the twelve conjugates of W, and that group is exactly the image of the alternating group on five letters acting on its six Sylow-five subgroups. Hence the packet-preserving permutations form a group of order one hundred twenty, generated by the three displayed label permutations, and equal to the normalizer of that alternating image. The fifteen pairs of labels are also identified with the fifteen nonzero heart vectors: the heart vector of a pair of distinct labels is nonzero, every nonzero heart vector is the heart vector of such a pair, and the heart matrix of a label permutation carries the heart vector of a pair to the heart vector of the permuted pair. Two nonzero heart vectors have the same matching index exactly when the second is the first, the first multiplied by W, or the first multiplied by W+1, so the five matchings of the displayed one-factorization are exactly the orbits of multiplication by W. Consequently a permutation of the six labels carries every matching of that one-factorization to a matching exactly when conjugation by its heart matrix carries W to W or to W+1, and it centralizes W exactly when it both preserves the one-factorization and is an even permutation of the six labels. Preserving the displayed one-factorization is therefore the packet-preserving condition and is strictly weaker than centralizing W.
