It proves the two ways that step meets an orthogonal decomposition: a block-diagonal matrix is self-adjoint for a block-diagonal inverse Gram matrix as soon as each block is, so separate lifts assemble and the decomposition is preserved, and a scalar matrix is self-adjoint for every inverse Gram matrix, so a lift extends by a scalar on the complementary summand. Finally, Lean proves that the unimodular summand carries no discriminant: the constant vector lies in the image of 6I5-J5, has value five under the form, the value of the chart's first coordinate line, every integral vector is congruent modulo that image to a combination of the four remaining reduced basis vectors, whose Smith entries have exact depth one at two and at three, and six annihilates the quotient, so at either prime dividing six the primary part is supported on those four coordinates. Over any coefficient ring in which five has an inverse, Lean also proves the decomposition itself as a change of basis: the chart matrix is invertible, its first column is the first coordinate vector and its other columns are the displayed complement vectors, and it carries 6I5-J5 to the block matrix with the unit line of value five and the complementary block (6/5)(5I4-J4). The first chart dual vector is then in the image of the form and every vector is congruent modulo that image to a combination of the four chart dual vectors orthogonal to it. Lean also proves the chart decomposition in the form the split presentation consumes: the chart Gram matrix has value five on the first coordinate line, vanishes between that line and the other four coordinates, and equals the uniformizer times the unit multiple of 5I4-J4 on those four coordinates, and that block is symmetric with an explicit two-sided inverse, so the depth-one summand is unimodular after division by the uniformizer. The depth-one lifting construction is then instantiated at that exhibited block rather than at a supplied invertible Gram matrix. In the split coordinates, the chart coordinates followed by a supplied change of basis of the depth-one summand, the six-axis form is again the unit line of value five orthogonal to the depth-one part, whose block is the multiple 6/5 of the transported block; and two depth-one coordinates that are eigenvectors of a slope self-adjoint for 5I4-J4, with cancellable eigenvalue difference, pair to zero, which is the step making the eigenblocks orthogonal summands. For the three-primary case Lean also derives the split form itself: a slope whose reduction modulo the uniformizer is scalar equals that scalar plus the uniformizer times an integral error term, assembled from the divisibility witnesses of the entries with nothing divided, and for a slope in that form the split-slope commutator of the descent conditions is the commutator of the coefficient block with the actual slope, so the depth-one blocks impose the manuscript's descent condition on the slope itself.
claims.cautions: The two residue-field matrices are explicit algebraic models only. The concrete finite-etale theorem constructs the quadratic splitting extension of F2 for the displayed companion-block model and transports its marked root to one member of the two-element Frobenius orbit outside {0,1} in F4; the two exotic scalars are not otherwise individually named. It does not construct or identify the manuscript's marked geometric splitting extension. Lean does not prove that the actual six-axis geometric principal kernel or quotient graph has either model as its slope, does not identify the actual three-primary slope with a one-point finite-etale block, and does not prove persistence through the connected smooth component. Thus the geometric assertions about the actual kernels and slopes remain unformalized. The two finite F2 checks use ordinary kernel reduction via decide, with no native-code decision procedure, external certificate, or oracle; all remaining model claims are symbolic kernel-checked proofs. The passage from determinant prime-to-p to the formal Z_p notion of a unimodular lattice is represented arithmetically rather than through a dedicated p-adic lattice structure. The two clauses that previously had neither a terminal nor a fragment are now covered, at the strength of the algebra they state. The lifting terminal is about matrices over a ring: it does not identify the residue endomorphism with the slope of a geometric principal kernel, and the manuscript's separate reduction step at three, surjectivity of Sp_2(Z_3) onto Sp_2(F_3) used to lift a complementary symplectic ruling, is not formalized. The lift itself is the elementary construction that runs in the manuscript's text between statements, so no statement digest covers that text. For the discriminant the manuscript's summand is realized in the chart itself, over any coefficient ring in which five is invertible, which covers the two-adic and three-adic cases it uses; the parallel statement over the integers is recorded through the Smith reduction, whose unimodular coordinate has the constant vector as its reduced basis vector, also of value five, and is a different line from the chart's. Lean does not identify the discriminant group of the coefficient matrix with a geometric isogeny kernel. The passage from these data to the split-block form consumed by the all-degree graph saturation theorem is now formalized at coefficient level, and is recorded with the six-axis divided-power row: the split coordinates, depths, scalars, and slope errors are constructed from the chart rather than supplied. What remains supplied there is the eigenblock decomposition itself, through the change of basis of the depth-one summand and the scalars and error terms of the split slope, together with every geometric datum: no principal kernel, slope of an actual kernel, idempotent lifting over a complete ring, or reduction of the symplectic ruling at three is constructed. The split form is proved only in the case where the residue is scalar, which is the three-primary one; the two-primary case needs the eigenblock decomposition of an exotic slope over an unramified quadratic extension, and Lean separately records that no such slope exists over an ordered coefficient ring, so it cannot be exhibited by an integral matrix.

claims.objects: Lean represents a weighted matrix-of-ideals lattice, its internal rank-one span, a square-zero additive realization in a commutative ring, an abstract integral product subgroup, and explicit natural-number denominator witnesses for the resulting squarefree product representative. The chart terminal adds the five-dimensional coefficient lattice of the local chart, its split coordinates distributed over the unimodular line and the blocks of the depth-one slope, the composite change of basis over the splitting ring, and the depth, scalar, and slope-error families attached to them.
claims.hypotheses: The lattice is exactly rank-one generated; every internal rank-one realization squares to zero; and for every prime p and every relevant finite internal presentation, some multiplier not divisible by p carries its squarefree degree-k product into the integral product subgroup. This is the elementwise denominator condition needed by the manuscript's local-to-global step; finite generation is unnecessary once these witnesses are supplied. The chart terminal is over a faithfully flat extension of the base coefficient ring which is a discrete valuation ring in which five is invertible, with the uniformizer irreducible there, a supplied invertible change of basis of the depth-one summand, a supplied identification of the depth-one blocks with the four remaining chart coordinates, supplied slope scalars and integral error terms, and the three graph-coordinate descent conditions for exactly those data. Its geometric inputs are explicit typed premises: the cohomological realization of coefficient matrices, an injective pullback to the elliptic-power source compatible with it, the divisor submodule, and the compatibility of the class and of its divided power with that realization.
claims.conclusion: A finite internal rank-one presentation exists whose degree-k squarefree product belongs to the integral product subgroup globally and whose factorial multiple equals the kth power of the realized lattice element. Instantiated at the local chart, Lean proves the same conclusion with the split presentation built from the chart instead of supplied: the coordinates are the chart coordinates followed by the change of basis of the depth-one summand, the depth is zero on the unimodular line and one on every depth-one block, and the scalars and error terms are those of the split slope. Every divided power of a class satisfying the descent conditions for those data is an ordinary integral divisor product, and its factorial multiple is the corresponding power of the class.
claims.cautions: The six-axis graph divisor lattice, its realization in cohomology, the comparison away from six, production of the denominator witnesses from localization, and identification of divided powers with ordinary divisor products are not formalized here. In particular Lean does not yet prove membership of Theta^4/4! or any geometric divided-power claim, and the special-fibre Neron-Severi caution remains geometric. The local chart is now formalized at coefficient level and feeds the split-graph saturation theorem directly, so the depths, scalars, slope errors, and coordinates of that instantiation are constructed rather than supplied; the eigenblock decomposition of the depth-one slope, the geometric realization, and the identification of the resulting product with the principal polarization remain supplied or absent.

claims.objects: A parameter type, a typed family of cubic-threefold objects, a separate type of intermediate-Jacobian objects, the intermediate-Jacobian assignment, predicates for smooth complex cubic status, algebraicity of the primitive minimal class, and universal CH0-triviality.
claims.hypotheses: Every indexed fibre is a smooth complex cubic threefold; the primitive minimal class of every fibre's intermediate Jacobian is algebraic; and for every smooth cubic under consideration Voisin's criterion identifies primitive-minimal-class algebraicity with universal CH0-triviality.
claims.conclusion: Every indexed fibre is universally CH0-trivial.
claims.cautions: Lean proves only the universally quantified logical deduction. The cubic pencil, smooth fibres, intermediate Jacobians, primitive minimal classes, their algebraicity from the six-axis divided-power theorem, Chow groups, universal base change in the CH0 predicate, and Voisin's geometric equivalence are represented by supplied types, functions, predicates, and premises rather than constructed. The argument is fibrewise and asserts neither a horizontal cycle nor a relative decomposition of the diagonal. The deduction itself is one step: Voisin's equivalence is supplied as an iff for every smooth fibre, algebraicity of the primitive minimal class is supplied fibrewise, and the conclusion is their composition. Lean adds no mathematical content beyond checking that the premises compose.

claims.objects: A field in which two is invertible, a finite index type for the coordinates other than the distinguished one, a nonzero border vector in the role of the coefficient vector of the linear part of the defining form in adapted coordinates, a symmetric block in the role of the matrix of its quadratic part, the bordered symmetric matrix built from them in the role of the Hessian at the point, its matrix rank, and the symmetrized outer product of two vectors in the role of a quadratic form divisible by a given linear one.
claims.hypotheses: The border vector is nonzero, which is the smoothness of the hypersurface at the point in the adapted coordinates; the block is symmetric; and two is invertible in the coefficient field.
claims.conclusion: The bordered matrix has rank at most two exactly when the block is the symmetrized outer product of the border vector with some vector.
claims.cautions: A fragment.  Lean constructs no projective space, cubic form, hypersurface, smooth point, tangent hyperplane section, cone, or Eckardt point, and does not carry out the passage from a point of a smooth cubic threefold to the adapted normal form or the identification of the bordered matrix with the Hessian of the form.  The equivalence proved is the linear algebra behind the criterion, between matrix rank and divisibility of the quadratic part by the linear part, in the matrix form of both conditions.  The second assertion of the manuscript's lemma, that every smooth cubic threefold in the separated-variable class and in the coprime-degree family carries such a point, is not formalized: it needs the geometry the companion does not construct.

claims.objects: A smooth cubic threefold in P^4, its Eckardt points, and the reflections of GL_5(C), meaning the elements of order two whose fixed subspace is a hyperplane.
claims.hypotheses: Smoothness of the threefold and the Hessian rank criterion of the preceding lemma.
claims.conclusion: Sending a reflection that fixes the defining form to the line on which it acts by minus one is a bijection onto the Eckardt points of the threefold.
claims.cautions: Not formalized.  The statement is about the linear reflection, not about its class in PGL_5(C); of the two lifts of an Eckardt involution exactly one fixes the form, and it is the one with a single eigenvalue minus one.

claims.objects: A smooth cubic threefold in P^4 whose automorphism group acts irreducibly on C^5, its Eckardt points, and the finite complex reflection group generated by the reflections that fix its defining form.
claims.hypotheses: Smoothness, irreducibility of the automorphism action on C^5, the existence of one Eckardt point, and the Shephard-Todd classification of irreducible complex reflection groups of rank five together with their invariant degrees.
claims.conclusion: The threefold is projectively equivalent to the Fermat cubic threefold and carries exactly thirty Eckardt points.
claims.cautions: Not formalized.  The classification is imported, not proved here.  Irreducibility of the automorphism action is a genuine hypothesis: a separated-variable cubic threefold carries Eckardt points and its automorphism group preserves the splitting, so it acts reducibly.

claims.objects: The coarse-moduli image of the nonstandard invariant cubic pencil of the alternating group on five letters, the Eckardt points of its members, and the coprime-degree family of Yang, Yu and Zhu.
claims.hypotheses: Smoothness of the members, the Eckardt criterion of the preceding lemma, the reflection-group classification of the preceding proposition, and the automorphism group of the Fermat cubic threefold as an imported result.
claims.conclusion: Exactly two members of the pencil are smooth cubic threefolds carrying an Eckardt point; they are interchanged by the normalizer of A_5, each carries exactly thirty Eckardt points, and both are projectively equivalent over C to the Fermat cubic threefold, so they represent a single moduli point; every other moduli point is represented only by cubics with no Eckardt point, and in particular by none projectively equivalent to a member of that family.
claims.cautions: Not formalized.  The proof invokes no computation: the identification of the members is the reflection-group classification, and the count of two is a cohomological count of the complements to the diagonal subgroup of the Fermat automorphism group.  Their coordinates on the parameter line are recorded separately in lem:pencil-loci-coordinates, which nothing here uses.

claims.objects: The nonstandard A_5-cubic pencil in the six-point model, its Eckardt locus and its reduced locus of singular parameters as subsets of the parameter line.
claims.hypotheses: The Hessian rank criterion, the preceding proposition, and the registered elimination over Q.
claims.conclusion: In the chart where the coefficient of the power sum is one, the two members carrying an Eckardt point are the roots of b^2+3b+9 and the singular members are the roots of b(b+6)(b^2-3b-9)(7b^2+3b+9); the remaining pencil point is smooth with no Eckardt point.
claims.cautions: Not formalized.  Both loci come from Groebner eliminations over Q, trusted as executions of Singular rather than certificate-checked; the registered bundle tracks two independent cross-checks, the same eliminations over a large finite field and a separate enumeration over five small ones.  Nothing else in the manuscript depends on this lemma: it places the members of the preceding proposition in coordinates and does not enter its proof.

claims.objects: The concrete two-dimensional model of the two-primary coefficient heart over the four-element field, the trace-determinant pairing on it with values in the two-element field, the lines spanned by its vectors, and its subspaces over the four-element field.
claims.hypotheses: For the first statement: a nonzero vector, and vanishing of the pairing between every multiple of it and every multiple of a second vector, which is orthogonality of the two lines they span.  For the second: a subspace over the four-element field with at most two elements, which is the size a cyclic subgroup killed by two can have.
claims.conclusion: The second vector is a multiple of the first, so two orthogonal lines coincide and are never complementary; and a subspace with at most two elements is trivial.
claims.cautions: A fragment covering two algebraic steps of the proof, not the proposition.  Lean constructs no intermediate Jacobian, elliptic curve, abelian variety, isogeny, polarization, Hodge structure, or integral homology lattice, and does not identify the concrete model used here with the discriminant heart of the six-axis lattice.  The classification of the isogeny shape is not formalized: neither the passage from an odd-degree isogeny to an orthogonal decomposition of the heart into subspaces stable under the four-element field, nor the generator count bounding the dimension of the summand carrying the heart, nor the realization of the two-factor case by an axis, nor the final contradiction with the order of the heart.  What is checked is that the one-and-one pattern of that decomposition is impossible, and that a summand small enough to be cyclic of exponent two vanishes.  Nothing here asserts a polarization on any factor of the intermediate Jacobian or any lattice invariant of it.

claims.objects: A parameter type with a family of varieties, an opaque coarse-moduli type with a moduli map on the parameter type, predicates for carrying an Eckardt point and for being of separated-variable type, a relation of projective equivalence, a distinguished moduli point, and the derived property of being represented by a separated-variable cubic, meaning that some cubic of that type is projectively equivalent to the member.
claims.hypotheses: Three typed Eckardt-locus premises say that a cubic of separated-variable type carries an Eckardt point, carrying one is invariant under projective equivalence, and every family member carrying one has the distinguished moduli point. Existence at the distinguished point is represented by primitive data: a chosen parameter and model, equality of that parameter's moduli point with the distinguished point, separated-variable status of the model, and projective equivalence to the chosen fibre. The independently registered fibrewise universal CH0-triviality theorem is supplied on the same family.
claims.conclusion: The separated-variable locus of the family in coarse moduli is exactly the distinguished point, and every family member at another moduli point is universally CH0-trivial and has no separated-variable representative.
claims.cautions: Lean performs the transport of the Eckardt criterion, constructs the separated-variable existential from the primitive witness data, and composes the exclusion with the independently established fibrewise universal CH0 statement. The geometric Eckardt inputs, primitive witness data, and universal CH0 theorem are premises at this interface. No cubic form, Eckardt point, pencil, coarse moduli space, or projective equivalence is constructed; the moduli space is opaque and its points are compared only by equality.

claims.objects: The Euler and grading matrices derived in the manuscript from Beauville’s small quantum products for a cubic threefold, the constant separating basis, the normalized regular block gauge, and the rank-two zero block with its canonical elementary modification.
claims.hypotheses: A characteristic-zero field and a nonzero square root r of three times the line-class Novikov variable. Lean takes the two displayed matrices as data and checks the finite matrix and normalized-gauge calculations.
claims.conclusion: The Euler matrix has eigenvalues 6r, -6r, 0, 0 with one rank-two Jordan block at zero; the first two reduced coefficients and the modified residue have the displayed values and indicial polynomial; the normalized block gauge exists and is unique coefficientwise; and the resulting exponent difference 2/3 is not an integer.
claims.cautions: Fragment. Lean checks the algebraic reduction but does not derive the quantum products or identify the input matrices with the cubic QDM. That identification is now derived in the manuscript from Beauville’s published formulas. Higher gauge coefficients are established recursively rather than explicitly computed.

claims.objects: The square-zero part of the centered leading Euler operator of an even rank-two formal connection block, the coefficient family of the horizontal Poincare pairing in a chosen frame, and the coefficient family of the connection in the loop direction, all as two-by-two matrices over a field in which two is invertible, together with the coefficients of the sesquilinear horizontality identity built from them.
claims.hypotheses: The leading operator part squares to zero and is nonzero, and the leading pairing coefficient is invertible. Horizontality enters either as the two displayed matrix equations -- self-adjointness of the leading operator part for the leading pairing coefficient, and the constant coefficient relating the regular coefficient, the two leading pairing coefficients, and the leading operator part -- or, in the derived form, as vanishing of the coefficients of the loop-direction horizontality identity at the order of the inverse loop coordinate and at the constant order.
claims.conclusion: The coefficient of the inverse loop coordinate is exactly self-adjointness of the leading operator part, and the constant coefficient is exactly the four-term relation; from those, the regular coefficient carries the nilpotent line into itself, in the equivalent matrix form that the leading operator part, the regular coefficient, and the leading operator part again have vanishing product, together with its vector form: every vector in the image of the leading operator part is carried into its kernel.
claims.cautions: Lean does not construct the A-model F-bundle, the spectral cover, the rank-two formal connection block, or the Poincare pairing, and does not prove nondegeneracy of the pairing on a separated spectral block; those supply the hypotheses. Horizontality of the pairing is represented as vanishing of the coefficients of a formal identity between matrix coefficient families, not as a property of a geometric connection. The line is presented as the image of the leading operator part rather than as a subobject of a geometric bundle.

claims.objects: The connection of a centered rank-two factor as a formal object: the loop and base connection matrices, each with a simple pole, are represented by the power series obtained from them by clearing that pole, so that flatness and horizontality of the sesquilinear pairing are single identities of formal power series with matrix coefficients; the canonical elementary modification, constructed as the gauge diag(1, u) and applied to both directions without inverses or Laurent series; the residue of the modified lattice and its discriminant, the square of the trace minus four times the determinant; a map of the coefficient ring that is additive and satisfies the Leibniz rule, applied entrywise, modelling a base vector field; and, for the germ statement, the ring of multivariate formal power series in the coordinates of the germ over a field of characteristic zero, with its formal partial derivatives as the coordinate directions.
claims.hypotheses: The frame is adapted: the leading coefficient of the loop direction is the square-zero matrix whose only nonzero entry is an invertible upper-right entry, the unit coming from the leading Euler operator. Two is invertible in the coefficient ring, which over the germ ring is automatic. The pairing is horizontal for the loop direction and its leading coefficient has invertible determinant, which is nondegeneracy in the form the germ ring supports; and the pair of connection matrices is flat, in every coordinate direction for the germ statement. The two final terminals instead assume the coefficient equations directly: for the first, that the upper-right entry of the residue is invertible and that the order minus-one coefficient of flatness in the modified lattice vanishes; for the second, that the entrywise derivation carries the residue to its commutator with a supplied regular matrix.
claims.conclusion: Flatness forces the leading coefficient of the modified base direction to vanish, so the modified connection is regular in that direction; the next order of flatness is then the Lax equation, with the regular coefficient of the modified base direction itself as the conjugating matrix rather than a supplied one; consequently every derivation of the coefficient ring annihilates the residue discriminant, and over the germ that discriminant equals the constant series with its own constant coefficient, so it does not vary over the germ. Horizontality of the pairing, not an assumption on the connection, supplies the property of the regular coefficient that the modification needs. The two final terminals record the same vanishing of the residual pole and the same annihilation of the discriminant from the supplied coefficient equations alone.
claims.cautions: The geometry is not constructed and remains the input, exposed as typed premises: that a rank-two formal connection block of the A-model F-bundle supplies a connection of this shape in an adapted frame, that the Poincare pairing of that block is the horizontal pairing of the connection, and that the formal power-series model computes the germ of the spectral component. Lean builds no F-bundle, spectral cover, connected component of one, or geometric lattice, and the centering of the scalar irregular part is part of the presentation rather than a formalized step. Constancy is proved over the formal germ, not analytic local constancy on a rigid chart.

claims.objects: The residue of the canonical modified lattice as a two-by-two matrix over a commutative ring, together with two ring elements presented as its eigenvalues through its trace and determinant.
claims.hypotheses: The trace of the residue is the sum of the two supplied elements and its determinant is their product, which is what splitting the characteristic polynomial supplies.
claims.conclusion: The residue discriminant is the squared separation of the two eigenvalues, and it is unchanged by adding a scalar multiple of the identity to the residue, so it is insensitive to a scalar normalization.
claims.cautions: Only the second assertion of the proposition is formalized. The identification of the eigenvalue classes modulo the integers with the formal exponent classes of the centered rank-two module rests on the formal classification of regular-singular differential modules, which Lean does not construct, and the meromorphic gauge implementing the modification is not represented.

claims.objects: Lean represents a supplied finite complex matrix declared to be the framed formal-monodromy operator; it does not construct the small even quantum connection or its Levelt--Turrittin monodromy.
claims.hypotheses: The matrix is already the operator for one turn of the original unramified z-disc, on a labelled finite-dimensional complex vector space.
claims.conclusion: The invariant is the sum of the characteristic-polynomial root multiplicities at exp(pi*i/3) and exp(-pi*i/3).
claims.cautions: The type records the framed operator only after construction; it neither permits nor models adjoining roots of z, and it does not prove independence of the algebraic closure.

claims.objects: For the identity shift: a commutative solution algebra with a ring automorphism in the role of one turn of the original loop coordinate, an invertible square matrix over it in the role of a fundamental solution frame, an invertible scalar of that algebra in the role of the irregular twist, and a constant matrix in the role of the framed monodromy of a frame.  For the divisor shift: two square complex matrices in the roles of the framed monodromy before and after the shift, a ring endomorphism of the complex numbers in the role of the coefficient substitution, an invertible frame gauge, and the sum of the algebraic multiplicities of the two primitive sixth roots of unity in a characteristic polynomial.
claims.hypotheses: For the identity shift: the turn fixes the scalar, which is the single-valuedness of the twist on the original loop disc; the frame and the scalar are invertible; the constants embed injectively in the solution algebra; and both the frame and its twist satisfy the frame relation defining their monodromy.  For the divisor shift: the shifted monodromy is the substituted original one conjugated by an invertible frame gauge; the substitution is injective and fixes both primitive sixth roots of unity, as one fixing the complex numbers does.
claims.conclusion: The twisted frame has the same framed monodromy matrix as the original frame, hence the same characteristic polynomial and the same eigenvalues; and the shifted framed characteristic polynomial has the same primitive-sixth multiplicity as the original.
claims.cautions: A fragment, on both clauses.  Lean constructs no quantum connection, no bulk point, no Euler field, no string or divisor equation, no exponential twist, and no Novikov coefficient ring, so neither clause is about the shifted connection of the manuscript.  The identity-shift clause replaces the irregular twist by an arbitrary invertible scalar that the turn fixes, and the solution algebra by an arbitrary commutative ring with a ring automorphism; single-valuedness is a hypothesis, not a property of an exponential.  The divisor-shift clause takes the comparison of the two monodromy matrices as a supplied datum rather than deriving it from the divisor equation, and takes the substitution's fixing of the two primitive sixth roots as a hypothesis rather than deriving it from an embedding of coefficient fields over the complex numbers.  The manuscript's statement is about all roots of unity; the formal statement covers an arbitrary fixed root for a single polynomial and the primitive sixth roots for the framed multiplicity.

claims.objects: Three nested algebraic branches are represented. The general coefficient-pushforward branch has effective homological and numerical additive monoids, a possibly nonsurjective quotient, compatible natural-number-valued degree functions, finite bounded homological pieces, and ordinary or completed coefficient families. The completed-convolution branch has one additive monoid with an additive natural grading, finite bounded pieces, and compatible systems of finite additive-monoid-algebra truncations. The completed numerical-ring branch adds finite bounded numerical pieces, a surjective degree-compatible quotient, finite coefficient packets, and additive scalar-weight homomorphisms for logarithmic Novikov operators.
claims.hypotheses: In the general branch, ordinary pushforward uses additive-commutative-monoid coefficients, while completed additive pushforward uses additive-commutative-group coefficients; its elementary cutoff-agreement theorem assumes equality of the two source families through the chosen cutoff. The convolution, `AgreeThrough`, and cutoff-continuity terminals use commutative-ring coefficients. The finite-packet terminal uses additive-commutative-monoid coefficients and explicitly assumes that its coefficient function is constant on numerical fibers. The compatible-family pushforward terminal assumes a surjective quotient with exact degree compatibility, finite bounded gradings on both sides, and commutative-ring coefficients. The standalone Leibniz terminal assumes one finite-degree additive monoid, commutative-ring coefficients, and an additive scalar weight. Its numerical pushforward-commutation terminal additionally supplies an additive numerical weight whose homological weight is the quotient pullback.
claims.conclusion: Ordered additive decompositions are finite and exact; convolution gives completed coefficient families a commutative-ring structure and agrees through every cutoff with ordinary additive-monoid-algebra multiplication. Completed coefficient families are equivalent, by mutually inverse reconstruction maps, to compatible systems of finite degree truncations. Under this equivalence, numerical pushforward is levelwise the ordinary additive-monoid-algebra map induced by the quotient, and the completed/truncation square commutes exactly. Addition, convolution, and numerical pushforward preserve coefficient agreement through the same cutoff, so numerical pushforward satisfies the explicit cutoff-continuity predicate with identity modulus. Finite-fiber numerical summation preserves finite-below support and cutoff agreement, commutes exactly with finite truncation, preserves convolution and the unit, and defines a unital ring homomorphism. Finite coefficient packets constant on numerical fibers descend termwise and fiber sums are cardinality multiples of the descended coefficient. The coefficientwise operator associated to an additive scalar weight is an additive homomorphism and satisfies the Leibniz rule for completed convolution; completed pushforward commutes with this operator when the weight factors through the quotient.
claims.cautions: The general coefficient-pushforward quotient need not be surjective. The completed numerical pushforward is proved to be a ring homomorphism when its monoid quotient is surjective; Lean does not assert that this ring homomorphism is itself surjective. The formal completed rings are coefficient families with a finite-below support condition. Their explicit compatible-truncation object and type equivalence are coefficientwise. Cutoff continuity is a quantified coefficient-agreement predicate, not Mathlib topological continuity; no topology, uniform space, categorical limit cone, or universal property in a category of topological rings is represented. The finite-type Chow-variety proof of bounded finiteness is supplied as a hypothesis rather than formalized. Lean assumes rather than proves numerical invariance of the finite coefficient packet, and it does not identify that packet with Gromov--Witten invariants. The weighted operator is packaged additively but is not bundled as a scalar-linear derivation over a separately modeled coefficient subring. Quantum products and connections, curve pushforward and normal-bundle pairings, geometric construction of the additive curve-pairing weights, and base change of the quantum comparison isomorphisms are not represented.

claims.objects: A rank-two cluster over a formal power-series germ, presented by matrices over that ring: the leading operator as a scalar plus a traceless nilpotent part, the grading operator, a connection form in a chosen frame, the compression of quantum multiplication in each base direction, and the residue of an elementary modification.
claims.hypotheses: The coefficient field is of characteristic zero, the nilpotent part has an invertible off-diagonal entry and vanishing determinant at the closed point, the compressed multiplications commute with the leading operator and satisfy the compressed flatness identity, and, for the residue, each formal partial derivative is its commutator with a matrix regular in the germ.
claims.conclusion: The nilpotent part stays square-zero and nonzero over the germ, the residue has a characteristic polynomial with coefficients constant on the germ, and two blocks with the same monic split exponent polynomial have the same framed primitive-sixth multiplicity.
claims.cautions: Fragment.  Lean constructs no quantum connection, Euler operator, spectral projector, or elementary modification, and does not prove that a compression of a connection to an isolated cluster satisfies the displayed identities.  The germ is modelled by a multivariate formal power-series ring rather than an analytic or rigid-analytic germ, and the passage from residue eigenvalues to the exponents of framed monodromy is not formalized: the multiplicity statement takes the exponent multiset as data.

claims.objects: A supplied type of geometric objects with relations for a rank-r projective bundle and a codimension-c smooth-center blowup; dependent numerical Novikov specializations; and intrinsic and specialized finite-dimensional complex framed-monodromy matrices.
claims.hypotheses: For r at least two, the projective-bundle relation is supplied together with equality of its intrinsic characteristic polynomial to the r-th power of the base polynomial. For c at least two, the blowup relation is supplied together with c-1 center specializations and equality of the total characteristic polynomial to the ambient polynomial times the finite product of the specialized center polynomials.
claims.conclusion: Lean proves the exact framed operation formulas: projective-bundle primitive-sixth multiplicity is r times the base multiplicity, and blowup multiplicity is the ambient multiplicity plus the sum of the c-1 specialized center multiplicities.
claims.cautions: The result is conditional on the geometric and characteristic-polynomial comparison inputs. Lean does not construct varieties, vector bundles, projective bundles, smooth centers, blowups, endpoint or specialized-center quantum connections, Iritani comparison coordinates, parity restrictions, numerical Novikov specializations, or the characteristic-polynomial block identities. No loop-coordinate root is represented.

claims.objects: Lean represents an effective additive monoid, a complete separated topological commutative domain, a multiplicative monomial-image function, a natural-number-valued length, and a natural-number-valued valuation.
claims.hypotheses: The monomial image preserves zero and addition, every monomial image is nonzero, valuation equals length on monomials, length is positive off zero and proper on bounded sets, and valuation is additive on products of nonzero target elements.
claims.conclusion: A typed certificate for the algebraic and topological core of strict Novikov admissibility.
claims.cautions: Lean does not construct the numerical Novikov completion or the associated graded ring; global valuation multiplicativity records the no-product-cancellation input but is not yet proved equivalent to the manuscript's domain associated-graded condition.

claims.objects: Complex matrix models of the specialized small even connection: an integral weight function recording the eigenvalues of the grading operator, a residue matrix, a parity-correction matrix, the matrix of Euler multiplication of a projective space, and finite-dimensional complex framed-monodromy matrices for a base curve, a rank-two projective bundle over it, and its specialization.
claims.hypotheses: For the nef-canonical case, every nonzero entry of the residue raises the weight of its column by at least one, the parity correction has square one and commutes with the residue, and the framed monodromy is the parity correction times the exponential of two pi i times the residue.  For the projective cases, the characteristic polynomial of Euler multiplication is the specialized quantum relation with nonzero line coefficient, and the conclusion of the multiplicity-one Euler block lemma is supplied as an implication from simplicity of the spectral blocks to identity framed monodromy.  For the ruled-surface case, the base carries the nef-canonical data, the intrinsic projective-bundle formula doubles the base count, and the specialized and intrinsic framed characteristic polynomials agree.
claims.conclusion: The specialized primitive-sixth count vanishes in all three cases.  Along the way Lean proves that a finite sum of weight-raising matrices raises the weight and that a weight-raising matrix on a finite index type is nilpotent, that the exponential of a nilpotent complex matrix differs from the identity by a nilpotent matrix, that a parity-corrected unipotent monodromy has only characteristic roots of square one, that the specialized quantum relation of a projective space is separable so that every maximal generalized eigenspace of Euler multiplication is at most one-dimensional, and that it has exactly the expected number of distinct roots.
claims.cautions: Conditional deduction.  Lean constructs no target variety, quantum connection, Euler multiplication, grading operator, Novikov specialization, or Levelt--Turrittin decomposition, and does not prove that a geometric framed monodromy has the displayed factorization or that a geometric Euler operator has the displayed characteristic polynomial.  Strict Novikov admissibility appears only through nonvanishing of the line coefficient in the projective cases; its role in making the specialized connection well defined has no formal counterpart.  The conclusion of the multiplicity-one Euler block lemma and the identification of the specialized ruled-surface module with the intrinsic one are typed premises rather than formalized arguments.

claims.objects: A supplied type of geometric objects with dependent strictly Novikov-admissible specializations and intrinsic, divisor-tagged, and specialized finite-dimensional complex framed-monodromy matrices, all over C; separately, the algebraic strict-Novikov certificate, an individual-class tag map, a finite injective vector family over an infinite characteristic-zero field, a completed coefficient family with finite support below every length cutoff, an injective integral divisor-pairing vector, an additive tagged-image map into an additive target, monomial initial coefficients, and direction-dependent initial-form detectors valued in one-variable formal power series.
claims.hypotheses: For every supplied strictly Novikov-admissible specialization, the final common-field polynomial equality resulting from the unformalized coefficient extension and algebraic-closure identifications is supplied, as is the final polynomial equality resulting from the unformalized divisor-equation formal bulk gauge. The individual-class theorem assumes that the tag separates numerical classes. The abstract finite-family theorem assumes an injective vector family over an infinite characteristic-zero field. For the completed tagging injection, the integral pairing vector is injective over an arbitrary characteristic-zero coefficient field; every monomial initial coefficient is nonzero; every direction detector sends zero to zero; and, for every nonzero completed series and integral direction, the detected initial form of its tagged image is supplied to equal the finite exponential-character combination on the formalized lowest support.
claims.conclusion: Lean proves equality of intrinsic and specialized primitive-sixth multiplicities and transfers intrinsic vanishing through every strictly Novikov-admissible specialization. It proves injectivity of the paired monomial/class tag on individual numerical classes. For every finite injective vector family, it chooses an abstract K-linear separator and proves finite exponential-character independence; for integral pairing families it constructs an integral direction. At coefficient level, every nonzero completed series has a nonempty finite lowest support and exponential-character noncancellation over every characteristic-zero field. From the supplied initial-form compatibility and nonzero monomial initial coefficients, Lean proves the tagged image of every nonzero series is nonzero, reflects zero, and is fully injective by applying noncancellation to differences.
claims.cautions: The vanishing result remains conditional on two final polynomial equalities over C. No source coefficient fields, common comparison field, embeddings, Polynomial.map scalar extension, or typed bulk-gauge witness occur in that theorem. The associated-graded tagging interface neither represents nor constructs the filtered target ring, associated graded ring, valuation, or geometric Novikov specialization. It supplies only proxy detector functions, their zero values, nonzero monomial initial coefficients, and the compatibility equality, and does not prove that they arise from the manuscript's filtered hypotheses. Lean proves the exact noncancellation and injectivity deduction from these proxy inputs. The individual-class injection alone does not imply completed-series injection; the latter uses the compatibility package. Construction of the integral divisors whose pairing vectors separate numerical curve classes, common algebraic closures, scalar extension of quantum connections, the divisor-equation bulk pullback, and compatible integral-loop-power finite-quotient gauges also remain unformalized. The strength of the row is uneven and the terminals should be read separately. Once the two final polynomial equalities are granted, the vanishing endpoint is immediate, because the primitive-sixth multiplicity is defined from the characteristic polynomial; that terminal carries no mathematical content beyond the equalities it assumes. The content of the row is in the other terminals: independence of finite families of exponential characters through an integral separating direction and a Vandermonde argument, nonemptiness and exact membership of the lowest-length support, and nonvanishing and injectivity of the tagged additive map from proxy detector data.

claims.objects: A supplied type of geometric objects with a predicate for points, smooth projective curves, and smooth projective surfaces; a nef-seed predicate; a named point and projective-bundle and point-blowup relations; dependent strictly Novikov-admissible specializations; and intrinsic and specialized finite-dimensional complex framed-monodromy matrices.
claims.hypotheses: Every selected object has a supplied inductive classification witness built from a nef seed, the point, a positive-rank projective bundle, or a point blowup. Nef-seed characteristic roots are supplied to have square one; the point multiplicity is zero; the projective-bundle formula multiplies the base multiplicity by the rank; point blowup preserves multiplicity; and divisor tagging transfers intrinsic vanishing to each strictly Novikov-admissible specialization.
claims.conclusion: For every supplied point, smooth projective curve, or smooth projective surface and every strictly Novikov-admissible specialization, the specialized framed monodromy has primitive-sixth multiplicity zero. Lean proves the classification induction, including the exact root-square-one spectral endpoint, and the final specialization transfer. A separate corollary proves that matrix involutivity is a stronger sufficient condition for the spectral restriction.
claims.cautions: The result is conditional on every geometric and comparison input used by the human proof. Lean does not construct the varieties, quantum connections, framed monodromy, numerical Novikov rings, grading operator or parity correction; prove regular singularity and nilpotence of the residue; derive the plus-or-minus-one spectrum from nefness; prove the low-dimensional minimal-model classification; construct the projective bundles or blowups; establish their monodromy formulas; or prove divisor tagging and specialization comparison. The human proof restricts eigenvalues to {1,-1}; it does not assert involutivity of the full monodromy matrix, which is strictly stronger in the presence of possible Jordan parts and appears only in the separately marked sufficient corollary. The manuscript now uses divisor tagging only for surface centers that are neither minimal nor geometrically ruled; Hirzebruch surface targets are covered by the direct specialized argument, whose formal content is recorded under prop:hirzebruch-specialized-vanishing. The Lean statement retains divisor tagging as one typed premise of the classification witness and does not distinguish the two cases.

claims.objects: The free commutative monoid of framed-block isomorphism classes, whose blocks retain a marked small section and original-loop monodromy, its natural-number-valued additive primitive-sixth marker, smooth projective varieties in a fixed ambient dimension at most four, smooth centers with their individual specialized QDM summands, and one-projective-line stabilizations of threefolds.
claims.hypotheses: Regular isomorphism preserves primitive-sixth multiplicity; the residual hypotheses provide factorization data retaining each center summand separately and vanishing of every center contribution allowed in the fixed dimension; and the stabilization consequence additionally uses the rank-two projective-bundle formulas for both threefolds.
claims.conclusion: Birational smooth projective objects of any fixed dimension at most four have equal primitive-sixth marker. If two smooth projective threefolds become birational after multiplication by one projective line, their primitive-sixth markers are equal.
claims.cautions: Conditional deduction. Lean constructs the additive marker on the free commutative monoid, applies the general birational-descent theorem with each center summand retained separately, and cancels the factor two in the one-projective-line consequence. It does not construct the QDM comparisons, projective-bundle formulas, or the proofs that the separate center contributions vanish; those remain explicit typed inputs. The general theorem is registered separately under thm:marker-ledger.

claims.objects: A rank-one block presented by a one-by-one pairing and grading matrix, the compression of a commutator by a projector, the scalar equation of the block as a formal power-series equation, and the characteristic polynomial of a framed monodromy that is the identity.
claims.hypotheses: Two is invertible in the coefficient field, the pairing compressed to the block is nonzero, the grading operator is anti-self-adjoint there, the projector commutes with Euler multiplication and annihilates the first gauge coefficient on both sides, and, for the scalar equation, the coefficient field has characteristic zero.
claims.conclusion: The grading operator vanishes on the block, the order-`z` coefficient of the scalar equation vanishes, that equation has exactly one formal power-series solution with constant coefficient one, and a block whose framed monodromy is the identity contributes nothing to the primitive-sixth count.
claims.cautions: Fragment.  Lean constructs no quantum connection, Euler multiplication, Poincare pairing, Levelt--Turrittin decomposition, or splitting gauge, and does not derive the characteristic polynomial of the block's framed monodromy from the scalar equation; the unit contribution is proved for a polynomial that is a power of `X - 1`.

claims.objects: Framed formal-monodromy matrices of a smooth projective variety and of its product with a projective line, and their primitive-sixth multiplicities.
claims.hypotheses: The framed characteristic polynomial of the product is the square of that of the factor.
claims.conclusion: The primitive-sixth count doubles after product with a projective line.
claims.cautions: Conditional deduction. The Lean terminal is more general than the strict m=1 manuscript statement. Its premise is the conclusion of the manuscript's Levelt--Turrittin computation for the projective-line product, which rests on the Gromov--Witten product formula, numerical Novikov base change, the two distinct Euler eigenvalues of the projective line, and the multiplicity-one block lemma; none of those geometric inputs is constructed in Lean.

claims.objects: A supplied type of varieties with a distinguished point, the projective spaces, the product of a variety with a projective space, and the framed sixth-root count of each of them.
claims.hypotheses: The product formula multiplies the count of a variety by one more than the dimension of the projective factor; a projective space is the product of the point with that projective space; and the framed monodromy of the point is involutive.
claims.conclusion: Lean deduces that the point has vanishing count and hence that every projective space has vanishing count, including three-space and four-space.
claims.cautions: The product formula is a typed premise: Lean does not construct varieties, products, quantum connections, or framed monodromy, and does not prove the Gromov-Witten product formula or the compatibility of the formal decomposition with tensor products used in the manuscript's proof of that formula. Involutivity of the framed monodromy of the point stands for the manuscript's rank-one trivial connection at a point.

claims.objects: A supplied type of cubic objects with a smooth-complex-cubic-threefold predicate and a finite-dimensional complex framed-monodromy matrix; Cai's rank-two indicial polynomial and the displayed characteristic polynomial with one factor for each primitive sixth root and two unit factors.
claims.hypotheses: For every supplied smooth cubic threefold, the framed-monodromy characteristic polynomial is supplied to equal the displayed four-factor polynomial arising from Cai's integral-loop-power block description.
claims.conclusion: Lean proves the indicial roots -1/6 and -5/6 give the negative and positive primitive sixth roots, proves those roots are distinct and each has algebraic multiplicity one while the two unit factors contribute nothing, and concludes that every supplied smooth cubic threefold has primitive-sixth multiplicity exactly two. A second terminal reaches the same value from a weaker premise: it assumes only that framed monodromy exponentiates the exponents of the reduced system, with two unit factors from the rank-one blocks, and proves which exponents occur from the block reduction.
claims.cautions: The result is conditional on the characteristic-polynomial comparison. Lean does not construct a smooth cubic threefold, its numerical small even quantum connection, Cai's integral-loop-power block diagonalization, the rank-two zero-exponential block, the two remaining rank-one unit blocks, or the identification of their direct-sum characteristic polynomial with the supplied framed monodromy. Lean also does not prove that the cubic threefold's numerical curve lattice has rank one or that the manuscript's numerical-Novikov convention leaves Cai's calculation unchanged. The second terminal removes the characteristic-polynomial assumption in favour of the exponent-to-monodromy passage, which remains external; the exponents themselves are now derived from the displayed connection matrices.

claims.objects: Framed spectral data of the small even quantum connection of a smooth cubic threefold over a formal even bulk germ: a point of the germ carries a framed formal-monodromy matrix and the multiset of formal exponents of the rank-two zero cluster, together with the total rank of the clusters at the nonzero Euler eigenvalues.
claims.hypotheses: The framed characteristic polynomial at every point splits as the polynomial of the exponentials of the zero cluster's exponents times that power of `X - 1`, the exponent polynomial of the zero cluster is the same at every point as at the closed point, and at the closed point the framed characteristic polynomial is the displayed four-factor polynomial of the cubic packet.
claims.conclusion: The primitive-sixth multiplicity equals two at every point of the germ.
claims.cautions: Conditional deduction.  The germ is an arbitrary type with a distinguished point and the spectral data are supplied, so neither the coefficient-field extension making the square root of three times the line variable a unit, nor the quantum connection, nor the identification of the supplied rigidity with the formal-germ theorem proved for matrices over a power-series ring, is formalized.

claims.objects: A supplied type of varieties with a smooth-cubic-threefold predicate, framed monodromy, and the product of a variety with a projective space; the rank-two indicial polynomial of the reduced small even system.
claims.hypotheses: The product formula multiplies the count by one more than the dimension of the projective factor. The first terminal assumes the count of the base variety is two; the second assumes instead that framed monodromy exponentiates the exponents of the reduced system with two unit factors, and derives the value two from the block reduction.
claims.conclusion: The count of the product with a projective line is four; for the second terminal this holds for every supplied smooth cubic threefold.
claims.cautions: The product formula remains a typed premise, as does the passage from residue exponents to framed formal monodromy. Lean constructs neither the varieties and their products nor the quantum connections, and the companion's separate projective-bundle formula is proved only under the reconstruction-tail hypothesis registered with the conditional framed operation claim. The manuscript calls this statement unconditional in the sense that it does not assume Hypotheses 5.7R and 5.7T; that is independent of the typed premises recorded here, which are the imported product formula and the passage from residue exponents to framed monodromy.

claims.objects: An abstract geometric signature naming an object representing a smooth prime Fano threefold of genus eight, its associated Pfaffian cubic, both rank-two projectivizations, and the hypotheses of the rank-two formal-exponent marker argument.
claims.hypotheses: Each projectivization is birational to the one-projective-line product of its base, the two projectivizations are birational through the flop, rationality transports along the context's birational relation, and the associated cubic satisfies the hypotheses used in the one-stabilization marker theorem.
claims.conclusion: The product of the represented Fano threefold with one projective line is irrational.
claims.cautions: Conditional deduction. Lean constructs neither the Fano threefold, Pfaffian cubic, bundles, projectivizations, nor flop, and does not prove that a rank-two projectivization is birational to the corresponding product. No higher stabilization is represented.

claims.objects: An abstract geometric signature naming an object representing a smooth prime Fano threefold of genus eight, its associated Pfaffian cubic, both rank-two projectivizations, and the hypotheses for the framed primitive-sixth marker.
claims.hypotheses: The bases have dimension three, both projectivizations satisfy the rank-two marker formulas, the total spaces are birational through the flop, and the associated cubic has framed marker two.
claims.conclusion: The represented Fano threefold has primitive-sixth marker two.
claims.cautions: Conditional deduction. Lean applies framed marker invariance to the two projectivizations and cancels the common factor two, but constructs none of the geometric objects, the flop, the framed QDM comparisons, or the proofs that the center contributions vanish.

claims.objects: A leading-term map from a coefficient ring to a complex vector space of graded pieces, a family of monomials of that space indexed by an abstract type, and a map assigning to every effective class the index of its leading monomial.
claims.hypotheses: The family of monomials is linearly independent over the complex numbers, the leading term of zero vanishes, and the leading term of the image of every effective class is the monomial of its assigned index.
claims.conclusion: The reviewer-facing type of certificates that a specialization is monomial, in the form its consumers use.
claims.cautions: Lean constructs no completed monoid ring, no associated graded ring, and no Novikov specialization, and does not prove that the associated graded of the coefficient ring of a center specialization is a monoid algebra whose monomials form such a family. The type records the properties of the leading-term data that the arithmetic below consumes, not their geometric origin.

claims.objects: The two monic quartics displayed in the statement, in two complex parameters standing for the specialized values of the fibre class and of the section class shifted by the integer part of half the index in fibres, and the universal discriminant of a monic quartic in its coefficients.
claims.hypotheses: None beyond the displayed coefficients; the even splitting takes square roots of the two parameters.
claims.conclusion: Lean evaluates the universal quartic discriminant on the coefficients of each displayed quartic, obtaining two to the twenty-fourth times the square of the product of the two parameters and their difference in the even case, and minus the square of that product times the cube of the displayed quadratic in the odd case, and exhibits the even quartic as the product of the four linear factors with roots twice the four sums and differences of the square roots.
claims.cautions: The manuscript's conclusion is that these quartics are the characteristic polynomial of Euler multiplication on the even cohomology of a Hirzebruch surface. Lean constructs no variety, no quantum cohomology, no Novikov specialization and no Euler multiplication, and proves nothing about the deformation reduction to index at most one or about the toric presentation there; the quartics enter as displayed polynomials. The symbolic derivation of the quartics from the presented ring, together with its cross-checks, is the registered evidence bundle hirzebruch-euler-spectrum, generated by verification/hirzebruch_euler_spectrum.py and recorded in verification/hirzebruch-euler-spectrum.json.

claims.objects: A four-by-four complex matrix standing for Euler multiplication, its characteristic polynomial, the maximal generalized eigenspaces of the associated endomorphism, and a two-by-two complex matrix standing for a rank-two spectral block.
claims.hypotheses: The characteristic polynomial of the matrix is the displayed even or odd quartic; both specialized values are nonzero; off the degeneracy locus the corresponding separation hypothesis holds, that is the two values differ, respectively the quadratic in them is nonzero; on the locus the values are supplied in parametrized form, the common value as a square in the even case and as minus twenty-seven times the square of a scale parameter against sixteen times that parameter in the odd case; and for the rank-two statement the block has trace twice and determinant the square of a single eigenvalue.
claims.conclusion: Lean proves that the discriminant vanishes exactly when the two values agree in the even case and exactly on the displayed quadratic locus in the odd case; that off those loci every maximal generalized eigenspace has dimension at most one; that the odd parametrization covers its whole locus; that on each locus the quartic is a squared linear factor times a quadratic whose two roots differ from the repeated one; and hence that no maximal generalized eigenspace has dimension more than two, the one at the repeated root has dimension exactly two, and the two others have dimension exactly one. It also proves that the centered matrix of a rank-two block squares to zero.
claims.cautions: The identification of the algebraic multiplicity of an eigenvalue with the dimension of the maximal generalized eigenspace is proved for the supplied matrix; that the supplied matrix is Euler multiplication of a Hirzebruch surface is not. The odd degeneracy locus is parametrized by writing the section value as sixteen times a scale parameter, which is no restriction over the complex numbers and is recorded as a separate statement. Lean proves the nilpotent part of a rank-two block to be square-zero and does not prove such a block semisimple; the evidence bundle records the stronger computed fact that the block is semisimple at the degeneracy locus, which the manuscript does not use. The manuscript's closing sentence, that case (b) does not arise for a center specialization when the index is at least one while it can for the quadric surface, is a statement about the specializations of the blowup comparison and is recorded under lem:center-maps-monomial, lem:center-specialization-nondegenerate and prop:hirzebruch-specialized-vanishing, not here. The first of those three is absent from Lean, so at index one the graded-monomiality the closing sentence needs is argued in the manuscript only.

claims.objects: The algebraic core of a strictly Novikov-admissible specialization: an effective numerical monoid, a complete separated topological domain, the monomial image map, its length and valuation functions; and, for the third statement, a leading-term map together with a linearly independent family of monomials.
claims.hypotheses: The fibre class and the section class are nonzero, the shift is positive, and the two coefficients are units of the coefficient ring; for the third statement the leading term of the combination is the corresponding combination of two members of the family.
claims.conclusion: Lean derives from the valuation law that lengths are additive and multiples of a class have multiples of its length, that units and negatives leave a valuation unchanged, and hence that the specialized fibre value differs from the specialized shifted-section value and that no unit combination of the fibre value with the square of the shifted-section value vanishes. Independently of any shift, it proves that a combination of two members of a linearly independent family with coefficients two hundred fifty-six and twenty-seven cannot vanish, since for distinct members independence forces the first coefficient to vanish and for a common member the nonzero coefficient sum does.
claims.cautions: That the center specializations of the blowup comparison have this algebraic core, and that their associated graded is a monoid algebra whose monomials form a linearly independent family containing the leading term of every effective monomial, are manuscript statements about the geometry and are not formalized. The additivity of the leading-term map on two summands of equal valuation enters as a hypothesis.

claims.objects: Framed monodromy matrices with their primitive-sixth multiplicity, a four-by-four complex matrix standing for Euler multiplication on the even cohomology of the surface, and two two-by-two matrices standing for Euler multiplication on the two projective-line factors of the quadric surface.
claims.hypotheses: The characteristic polynomial of Euler multiplication is the displayed quartic, or, for the quadric surface, is the specialized quantum relation of a projective line on each factor; both specialized values are nonzero; the even or odd separation hypothesis holds, that is the two values differ, respectively the quadratic in them is nonzero; and the conclusion of the multiplicity-one Euler block lemma is supplied, in the tensor form for the quadric surface and in the direct form otherwise.
claims.conclusion: Lean proves that the Euler spectra are simple, applies the supplied implication to obtain a framed characteristic polynomial that is a power of the linear polynomial with root one, and concludes that the primitive-sixth multiplicity vanishes.
claims.cautions: No variety, product, quantum connection, Novikov specialization or Levelt--Turrittin decomposition is constructed. The Gromov--Witten product formula, the compatibility of the formal decomposition with tensor products, and the multiplicity-one Euler block lemma enter as hypotheses; the quadric statement assumes no relation between the two specialized values, which is what makes it cover the specializations identifying the two rulings.

claims.objects: An additive monoid of center degrees, an additive monoid of target exponents, the additive exponent map between them, and the additive-monoid algebra over the complex numbers on the target exponents.
claims.hypotheses: The exponent assignment is supplied as an additive-monoid homomorphism. No geometric or filtered-ring hypothesis is encoded.
claims.conclusion: Lean sends each center degree to the coefficient-one monomial at its supplied target exponent, proves that addition maps to multiplication, proves that the canonical target monomials are linearly independent, and packages these facts as monomial-specialization data with identity leading-term map.
claims.cautions: This is only the algebra after the exponent map has been supplied. Lean constructs no blowup center, numerical curve lattice, completed coefficient ring, filtration, associated graded of the manuscript's target ring, center specialization, or Iritani comparison, and therefore does not prove that the geometric specialization in the manuscript induces the supplied exponent map.

claims.objects: A finite free formal matrix system over a commutative coefficient ring, a finite coordinate labelling into spectral factors, a scalar attached to each factor, a block-diagonal leading operator equal to the scalar-label diagonal plus a nilpotent matrix, a normalized regular gauge, a reduced loop system, and the coefficient sequence of one base direction.
claims.hypotheses: Distinct factor scalars differ by units; the leading operator is block diagonal and differs from the scalar-label diagonal by a nilpotent matrix; and the base coefficients satisfy the recurrence extracted from flatness, namely that once all earlier coefficients are block diagonal, the commutator of the next coefficient with the leading operator is block diagonal.
claims.conclusion: Lean constructs a normalized regular gauge reducing the loop system, proves it and the reduced system unique coefficient by coefficient, and proves every coefficient of the base direction block diagonal in the same splitting.
claims.cautions: Fragment. Lean proves the formal Sylvester recursion and the coefficientwise flatness induction, but does not construct a quantum D-module, its generic coefficient field or algebraic closure, generalized-eigenspace subbundles, Novikov and bulk derivations, or the horizontal pairing. The paper supplies those geometric identifications and applies the same Sylvester argument separately to pairing horizontality.

claims.objects: Regular-isomorphism classes of typed blocks, their effective multisets, an additive marker valued in an arbitrary commutative additive monoid, abstract varieties and smooth centers, and a separately indexed family of specialized center summands.
claims.hypotheses: Assumed weak-factorization data and marker formulas supply blowup and blowdown chains in ambient dimension d, each blowup records its codimension and a separately indexed family of c-1 center summands, and every summand from a smooth center of dimension at most d-2 has zero marker contribution.
claims.conclusion: The marker is the unique additive extension of its value on each block class; birationally related endpoints have equal markers; and the marker descends to the quotient set of birational classes.
claims.cautions: Conditional deduction. Lean proves the free commutative-monoid construction, the arbitrary-monoid and arbitrary-dimension telescoping argument, preservation of the individual center summands, and descent to birational classes. Weak factorization and the geometric operation formulas are supplied as typed inputs rather than formalized from algebraic geometry. The QDM comparisons that produce those formulas remain outside this row and are registered under prop:qdm-operation-ledgers.

claims.objects: Iritani's divisor-equation-reduced completed coefficient ring for a blowup center, its combined Novikov-divisor generators, the independent center coordinates in the external direct-sum target, the common Laurent comparison ring, and the intrinsic generic even quantum D-module of the center together with its separately recorded scalar extensions in the center summands.
claims.hypotheses: Divisor pairings separate numerical curve classes; fibres of the untagged center monomial map are finite in every bounded ample-degree slice; the reduced source does not contain the independent target coordinates as coefficients; Iritani's reduced center connection and external direct-sum comparison are defined over the stated rings; and the combined bulk Jacobian is invertible.
claims.conclusion: The pullback from the reduced source to the external direct-sum target is injective because the exponential characters in the independent target coordinates separate every finite collision fibre. After passage to generic fraction fields, every center summand is a faithful scalar extension and formal reparametrization of the intrinsic generic numerical even QDM of the center.
claims.cautions: Fragment. Lean proves the completed-series injection from the stated initial-form hypotheses involving independent target coordinates, and the source type deliberately contains no target coordinate variables. It does not construct the geometric reduced source, the independent target coordinates, the completed filtrations and initial-form detector from Iritani's rings, the comparison and inverse, the bulk Jacobian, or the claimed QDM base-change diagram.

claims.objects: The generic QDM block decomposition on even cohomology, its effective block multiset, an additive marker, an integer suspension action on block classes, the corresponding multisets for varieties and individual center summands, a parity-preserving equivalence on full cohomology, and a finite multiplicity-preserving matching of transported block classes with a recorded degree shift on every pair.
claims.hypotheses: The comparison on full cohomology preserves the chosen even submodules in both directions. The additive marker is invariant under every recorded suspension. The projective-bundle matching identifies the total-space blocks with rank copies of the base blocks up to those suspensions. The blowup matching identifies the blowup blocks with the ambient blocks plus the literal finite family of individual center blocks, again up to recorded suspensions. Smoothness, positivity of the bundle rank, and the projective-bundle dimension formula are explicit premises of the packaged projective-bundle result.
claims.conclusion: Lean restricts the parity-preserving comparison to a linear equivalence on even cohomology, converts each suspension-compatible block matching into equality of additive markers, and derives the projective-bundle and blowup marker formulas with every center summand kept separate. It also packages the blowup formula with the center source and dimension data used in birational descent.
claims.cautions: Conditional deduction. Lean proves the restriction to even cohomology and the suspension-invariant categorical additivity step without identifying nonzero-degree maps with degree-zero graded morphisms. The formal blowup theorem keeps the source of every center summand visible. Lean does not construct cohomology or its parity splitting, the geometric QDM blocks, a fixed algebraic splitting field, the common coefficient ring, the parity-preserving regular comparison maps, pairwise spectral separation of summands, the invertible bulk Jacobians, or the component matching from Iritani's and Iritani–Koto's theorems; those remain the manuscript's cited geometric and analytic inputs.

claims.objects: The rank-two formal-exponent marker, smooth centers and their dimensions, individual specialized center summands in the QDM comparison, the intrinsic marker of a center, minimal surfaces with nef canonical class, projective two-space, ruled surfaces, positive-rank projective bundles, and point blowups.
claims.hypotheses: Every smooth center of dimension at most two is obtained from a minimal surface with nef canonical class, projective two-space, or a ruled surface by point blowups; the intrinsic formal-exponent marker vanishes in those initial cases, is multiplied by bundle rank, and is preserved by point blowup; and the marker of every individual center summand equals the intrinsic marker of its source center.
claims.conclusion: Every QDM center summand whose smooth source has dimension at most two has zero rank-two formal-exponent marker, exactly the vanishing premise needed for birational descent in dimension four.
claims.cautions: Conditional deduction. Lean proves the classification induction and its application to each individual center summand, but does not construct the geometric QDM blocks, classify the surfaces, prove the initial calculations or operation formulas, or construct the faithful comparison for each center summand.

Records the coefficient-ring scope of the two-primary depth-one slope. The depth-one block 5I4-J4 pairs a vector to the sum of the squares of its coordinates and of their pairwise differences, and the dual form (1/5)(I4+J4) to the inverse of five times the sum of the squares and the square of the coordinate sum, so both are positive semidefinite over a linearly ordered commutative ring and positive on the first coordinate vector; no matrix satisfying the relation of a primitive cube root of unity is self-adjoint for either. This proves only an obstruction over linearly ordered coefficient rings; it does not construct the two-primary slope over the complete unramified discrete valuation ring used in the manuscript.

States what the discriminant pairing of the six-axis source polarization is and that it is nondegenerate. On the classes of two integral vectors the pairing is the class modulo one of (1/6^8) times x^t adj(A) y, where A is the integral source polarization, so it vanishes exactly when 6^8 divides that integral numerator; and a class pairing to zero against every class is zero. The manuscript does not state these properties of the lattice pairing separately: it uses the commutator pairing of the polarized abelian scheme, which this package does not construct. The declaration is registered as machinery because it fixes the meaning of the pairing under which the isogeny-kernel row asserts maximal isotropy, and nondegeneracy is what makes an orthogonal complement the right notion there.
